conventions.note: Reference expressions are declared in .railway/railway.ts through the SDK's ref()/env accessors rather than written as strings, so a typo in a service name is a compile error rather than a variable that resolves to the literal text ${{Typo.VAR}}. The syntax above is what those accessors compile to, and is what verify_railway_configuration.ts asserts is still present on the live service.

ARPI_SITE_URL.purpose: Explicit canonical-origin override. Needed only for a custom domain, because RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN already answers for a Railway domain. Server-only by name: it must never be given a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix.

NEXT_PUBLIC_ARPI_CASE_STUDY_ENABLED.purpose: One of five conditions on the case-study gate. Absent, empty, malformed and unrecognised all resolve to false, so leaving it unset keeps the case study locked. It is set as a literal 'false' in the IaC to make the closed gate explicit on the service rather than merely implied by absence.

NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL.purpose: Retained only so an existing Vercel deployment keeps working. Ordered below RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN so a stale value cannot override the platform. Do not set it on Railway.

arpi-portfolio.forbiddenReason: The website has no database connection, no API key and no authentication provider. Any of these appearing on this service is a defect, not a configuration choice, and verify_railway_configuration.ts fails on it.

Postgres.note: Every variable on this service is published by Railway's Postgres template. None is authored here, none is copied anywhere, and POSTGRES_PASSWORD is generated by Railway rather than by this repository.

DATABASE_URL.resolvesTo: The private-network connection URL, including the generated superuser password.

ARPI_TCP_PROXY_DOMAIN.purpose: Recorded in the non-secret Fabric handoff. Never hardcoded.

ARPI_TCP_PROXY_PORT.purpose: Recorded in the non-secret Fabric handoff. Never hardcoded.

ARPI_PIPELINE_PASSWORD.purpose: Password for the arpi_pipeline login role, which holds arpi_loader. Generated by Railway, stored only in Railway, never printed and never written to a file.

ARPI_FABRIC_PASSWORD.purpose: Password for the arpi_fabric login role, which holds arpi_reporter and nothing else. This is the single credential a human later copies out of Railway into Microsoft Fabric.
ARPI_FABRIC_PASSWORD.rotationNote: Deliberately NOT rotated on every deployment. Rotating it would silently break a configured Fabric connection, and a credential that breaks a downstream consumer on every deploy gets replaced with a permanent one by whoever is on call. Rotation is a deliberate operation; see deployment/railway/README.md section 8.

ARPI_PROFILE.purpose: The deterministic profile. Seed and reporting window come from config/development.yaml, not from here.

ARPI_DATABASE__SSLMODE.purpose: TLS is required for the loader's own connection. The provisioning script additionally asserts the session is encrypted via pg_stat_ssl, because a setting in a variable proves nothing about the session that was opened.

ARPI_PROVISION_MODE.purpose: The job is safe to rerun: it applies the idempotent SQL sequence and re-verifies, and it never drops or recreates the database.

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.purpose: Graceful termination window. Set as a variable rather than a deploy field because that is the mechanism Railway's own Postgres template uses.

arpi-database-setup.forbiddenReason: The job needs no Railway credential. Every value it reads arrives as a reference variable resolved by the platform, and the passwords it needs are generated by the platform, so there is nothing for it to call the Railway API about.

sharedVariablesNote: None. A shared variable is the right tool when three or more services need the same value; here exactly one service consumes the database, so a direct service reference is both narrower and clearer about who depends on what.

RAILWAY_API_TOKEN.purpose: The only secret the bootstrap workflow needs. Account- or workspace-scoped, because project and service creation are account-level operations that a project-scoped token cannot perform.
RAILWAY_API_TOKEN.readFrom: environment variable only; never a command-line argument, never written to disk, never printed

githubActionsSecretsDeliberatelyAbsentRe: Railway either provides or can reference every one of these itself. Duplicating them into GitHub secrets would create a second copy of a credential with its own rotation problem, and a second place to leak it from.
